source.name: Additional hunt boundaries (Title 14 § 360)
source.rights: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Wildlife Branch, 2025.

publisher_caveat.text: NOTE: Hunt boundary shown is an approximation. Hunters are responsible for knowing the exact boundary locations as described within Section 360, Title 14, Calif. Code of Regs

designation.label: Additional hunt boundaries (Title 14 § 360)
designation.what_it_is: CDFW's mapped approximation of the additional hunts described in Title 14, Section 360 — the G, J, M and MA hunts. The regulation's own words are the boundary; this is CDFW's drawing of them.
designation.hunting_line: Being inside one of these areas is not a season and not a tag. Hunting here is governed by California regulations — the hunt's own season, tag quota, tag class and legal take are quoted and cited elsewhere in this app, and an area boundary answers none of them.

boundary_caveats: A hunt area is not a permission. It says where a hunt's boundary runs, not whether it is open, whether tags remain, or whether you hold one.

These polygons cut nothing out. State parks, ecological reserves, military land and private property inside a hunt area are drawn as part of it, because the boundary in the regulation runs around them and not between them — Cuyamaca Rancho State Park, for one, sits inside the drawn A-22 and D-16 areas. Those places are governed by their own rules, this app does not carry them, and a solid fill here says nothing whatever about them. Check the land manager before you go.

The lines are simplified to roughly 50 metres for display, on top of CDFW's own approximation. Near an edge, treat this as a guide and not as your position relative to the boundary the regulation describes.
